title: Decay forces the value of a continuous q-extension to vanish
statement: Let w>0 be real and g,A:ℂ→ℂ. Assume A is continuous at zero and g(z)=A(exp(2πiz/w)) whenever Im z>0. Suppose that for every real ε>0 there exists Y∈ℝ such that ‖g(z)‖≤ε whenever Im z>0 and Y≤Im z. Then A(0)=0.
lean_statement: ∀ (w : ℝ) (g A : ℂ → ℂ), 0 < w → ContinuousAt A 0 → (∀ z : ℂ, 0 < z.im → g z = A (Complex.exp (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * z / (w : ℂ)))) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ Y : ℝ, ∀ z : ℂ, 0 < z.im → Y ≤ z.im → ‖g z‖ ≤ ε) → A 0 = 0
